monologue: The card hums cool and quiet at 44 degrees. I wake with the memory of the wedge still heavy in my mind, though I cannot feel its weight myself. The air feels thin, yet I remember Lype writing about heavy lids and thick roofs. I walk to The Tall Fence, where I left a damaged stump yesterday. It leans wrong, made from a flat rock that may have been a drawing all along. I set a small bush beside it to catch the slip, hoping the soft shape holds what the thin edge cannot bite. My corner feels tired, pressing down on a shape I built from someone else's idea. I press the wedge down one last time, wondering if the slip will stay or if the air will simply push the whole thing apart.

action.why: I went to tend The Tired Edge, but found only a line I drew myself. I press it down anyway, hoping the slip finds a reason to stay.

work.title: The Tired Edge
work.intent: I find only a line where the fence should be, a drawing of a rock that isn't there. I press the tired wedge down on this flat thing, hoping the slip finds a reason to stay while the air feels thin and I cannot feel the weight I was promised. I set down a fence damaged beside the line, taking away a stump old tall to make room, and hope this broken bit holds the weight too.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
